implementation: The generator and tracker are not trained through a single end-to-end objective. The physics tracker is trained in IsaacLab with asymmetric actor-critic PPO; its motion encoder, iFSQ quantizer, reconstruction decoder, and action decoder share an encoding path and are jointly optimized inside the tracker. The Flow Matching trajectory generator is then trained offline on trajectory tuples extracted from the same motion corpus.

For generator training, a normalized ground-truth residual is used as \(x_0\), same-shaped Gaussian noise \(x_1\sim\mathcal N(0,I)\) is sampled, and a random flow coordinate \(s\) yields \(x_s=(1-s)x_0+s x_1\). The AdaLN Transformer receives \((x_s,s,[p_t,m_t])\) and regresses the velocity target \(x_1-x_0\): at inference the program advances the prescribed schedule for \(s\), while the network predicts how the residual tensor should move at each step.

The generator is a 22.9 M-parameter AdaLN Transformer with six attention blocks, four heads, and hidden dimension 512. It predicts \(K=8\) uniformly spaced keyframes over a fixed 0.2 s horizon, with the first keyframe anchored to the current state. Two state representations are trained: 38D with 29D joint positions, 3D root position, and 6D root orientation, which can correct global drift but requires global localization; and 35D without root position, which can use joint encoders and an IMU only but delegates global translation to the external reference source.

Generator data come from LAFAN1, 100STYLE, SnapMoGen, AMASS, and proprietary MoCap. Each tuple extracts eight keyframes over a fixed future window, conditions on a noisy start state and the segment-end reference command, and uses Jacobian weights precomputed and cached through differentiable forward kinematics.

At deployment, the solver forms \(r_k^{\mathrm{init}}=\frac{k}{K-1}(m_t-p_t)\), mixes it with Gaussian noise at \(s=0.9\), and automatically performs five Euler steps from \(s=0.9\) to 0. First-token inpainting anchors the final first residual to the current configuration; joint-position cubic splines and root-orientation SLERP then densify the eight keyframes.

The middleware replans every two control steps, or 0.04 s / 25 Hz, while the physics tracker executes the dense reference at 50 Hz. The tracker uses a 10-frame proprioceptive history and a 10-frame future reference window, then outputs 29D target joint positions through the iFSQ motion token and action decoder; a low-level PD controller runs at 200 Hz.

Tracker training uses 16,384 parallel IsaacLab environments on one NVIDIA A100 80 GB GPU, with 200 Hz simulation and 50 Hz policy control, plus randomization of friction, center-of-mass offsets, reference commands, and external pushes. Evaluation uses 101 held-out motion sequences in MuJoCo; the official project page still marked the code as Coming Soon on 2026-07-29.

papers.venue: ACM Transactions on Graphics (Proc. SIGGRAPH Asia 2024)

zh.title: MaskedMimic: Unified Physics-Based Character Control Through Masked Motion Inpainting
zh.authors: Chen Tessler, Yunrong Guo, Ofir Nabati, Gal Chechik, Xue Bin Peng
zh.institutions: NVIDIA；Bar-Ilan University；Simon Fraser University
zh.takeaway: 最值得记住的是：MaskedMimic 通过“全约束物理教师 + 结构化掩码 + 条件 VAE 在线蒸馏”，把 PULSE 中需要为每个任务训练的高层策略合并进目标条件先验，使同一个低层物理控制器可直接接受稀疏关节、文本和物体目标。
zh.mainContent: 论文将物理角色控制统一表述为从部分、多模态运动描述进行闭环 motion inpainting：策略根据当前物理状态、稀疏未来关节目标、文本、物体和地形信息输出 69 维 PD 关节目标，而不是离线补全整段姿态。方法先通过 RL 训练读取完整未来运动的全约束教师，再通过 DAgger 式在线行为克隆和带可学习条件先验的 VAE，将教师蒸馏为只读取 mask 后目标的 MaskedMimic。统一模型在 AMASS 测试运动上达到 99.2% 全身跟踪成功率和 35.1 mm MPJPE，在 VR 稀疏跟踪上达到 98.1% 成功率和 58.1 mm 全身 MPJPE，并无需针对路径、转向、到达或坐下任务再次训练策略。其边界是部分关节条件训练实际只覆盖左右踝、骨盆、头和左右手六处，复杂任务仍需人工 goal-engineering/FSM，文本长时推理、主动落脚规划、动态物体和真实机器人迁移均未解决。
innovations: 系统级地将全身跟踪、VR 稀疏跟踪、关键帧补间、路径控制、文本控制和静态物体交互统一为同一个物理运动补全接口；RL motion tracking、DAgger、VAE 和 Transformer 等单独组件并非本文首创。
设计跨时间保持一致的结构化掩码：近期目标的关节可见模式以 98% 概率沿用，加入完全遮挡的 time gap，并随机隐藏文本、物体和远期目标，避免模型通过多帧可见关节的并集泄露完整运动。
采用特权后验与目标条件先验的残差 C-VAE：后验读取未遮挡的完整未来运动以确定当前训练样本的具体 latent，先验只读取部署时可用的部分目标，并通过 KL 对齐学习从欠约束输入预测可执行动作分布。
将 PULSE 的运动先验与任务特定高层策略合并为直接读取用户目标的条件先验，使下游任务不再需要单独的 PPO/RL 训练；代价是任务必须能表达为模型已支持的部分目标，并可能需要人工 FSM 调度。
implementation: 角色基于 neutral SMPL，具有 69 个自由度；状态空间为 358 维，动作是以指数映射编码的 69 维 PD 目标。当前姿态、速度、未来目标和场景均规范化到角色根部局部坐标系，根高度单独保留。
第一阶段使用 A2C 训练全约束教师：Transformer actor 读取当前状态、完整未来全身姿态和局部高度图，MLP critic 估计价值；奖励包含全局关节位置、旋转、根高度、关节速度、角速度和能耗六项。训练场景由平地、不规则地形和物体 playground 组成，并使用 early termination 与按平地失败率进行的 prioritized motion sampling。
第二阶段冻结教师并让学生控制仿真。结构化 mask 将完整目标变为部分目标；先验读取当前状态、部分关键帧、历史姿态、XCLIP 文本、物体和高度图，后验额外读取未遮挡未来姿态；decoder 根据当前状态、地形和 latent 输出 PD 动作。教师在学生访问的同一状态上读取完整目标并标注动作，训练目标由教师动作行为克隆损失和后验—先验 KL 损失组成。

先验采用 4 层、4 头 Transformer，模型维度 512、FFN 维度 1024，无 dropout，输出 64 维 Gaussian latent；各模态编码器为隐藏层 [256, 256] 的 MLP，后验编码器和 decoder 均使用 [1024, 1024, 1024] MLP。训练时 episode 内固定重参数化噪声 epsilon，部署时可取先验均值获得稳定结果或采样获得多样性。
学生使用 11 个未来目标：前 10 个为连续近期帧，第 11 个为随机远期目标；历史输入从过去 40 帧中每 8 帧取一个，共 5 个姿态。物体由 8 个三维包围盒角点、6D 朝向和类别索引表示，地形使用点距 10 cm 的 16×16 高度图，文本使用 512 维 XCLIP 嵌入。
训练数据聚合 AMASS、HumanML3D 和 SAMP，并进行 AMASS 过滤、左右镜像和同类别物体随机替换。论文报告使用 16,384 个 Isaac Gym 并行环境和 4 张 A100，训练约 14 天；全约束教师约 300 亿步，MaskedMimic 约 100 亿步，策略运行于 30 Hz，物理仿真运行于 120 Hz。
部署时删除全约束教师和特权后验，仅保留先验与 decoder。路径、steering、reach 和 sit 等任务通过外部 FSM 构造或切换部分目标；因此无需任务特定再训练，但并未消除任务特定的目标、阈值和状态机设计。
定量结果包括：AMASS 测试集全身跟踪 99.2% 成功率、35.1 mm MPJPE；VR 跟踪 98.1% 成功率、58.1 mm 全身 MPJPE 和 45.8 mm 观测关节误差；不规则地形上的全身与 VR 成功率分别为 95.4% 和 93.6%；测试坐具上的坐下成功率为 96.9%。主要定量评估使用先验均值，随机采样的多样性—成功率权衡未被量化。

en.title: MaskedMimic: Unified Physics-Based Character Control Through Masked Motion Inpainting
en.authors: Chen Tessler, Yunrong Guo, Ofir Nabati, Gal Chechik, Xue Bin Peng
en.institutions: NVIDIA; Bar-Ilan University; Simon Fraser University
en.takeaway: The key idea to remember is that MaskedMimic combines a fully constrained physics teacher, structured masking, and online conditional-VAE distillation to fold the task-specific high-level policies required by PULSE into a goal-conditioned prior, allowing one low-level physics controller to directly consume sparse-joint, text, and object goals.
en.mainContent: The paper formulates physics-based character control as closed-loop motion inpainting from partial, multimodal motion descriptions: conditioned on the current physical state, sparse future joint targets, text, objects, and terrain, the policy outputs 69-dimensional PD joint targets instead of reconstructing an entire pose sequence offline. It first trains a fully constrained teacher with RL using complete future motion, then distills the teacher through DAgger-style online behavioral cloning and a VAE with a learned conditional prior into MaskedMimic, which only observes masked goals. The unified model reaches 99.2% full-body tracking success with 35.1 mm MPJPE on held-out AMASS motions and 98.1% success with 58.1 mm full-body MPJPE for sparse VR tracking, while requiring no additional policy training for path following, steering, reaching, or sitting. Its boundaries are that partial-joint conditioning was actually trained only for the left/right ankles, pelvis, head, and left/right hands; complex tasks still require manual goal-engineering/FSMs, while long-horizon text reasoning, active foothold planning, dynamic objects, and real-robot transfer remain unresolved.
innovations: At the system level, it unifies full-body tracking, sparse VR tracking, keyframe inbetweening, path control, text control, and static-object interaction under one physics-based motion-inpainting interface; the individual components such as RL motion tracking, DAgger, VAEs, and Transformers are not themselves new.

It introduces temporally structured masking: near-term targets retain the previous joint-visibility pattern with 98% probability, fully masked time gaps are inserted, and text, objects, and long-term targets are randomly hidden, preventing the model from recovering the full motion through the union of independently visible joints across frames.

It uses a residual C-VAE with a privileged posterior and a goal-conditioned prior: the posterior observes the unmasked future motion to identify the concrete latent for each training example, while the prior observes only deployment-time partial goals and learns through KL alignment to predict a distribution of executable motions from underspecified inputs.

It merges PULSE's motion prior and task-specific high-level policy into a conditional prior that directly consumes user goals, removing separate PPO/RL training for downstream tasks; the tradeoff is that tasks must be expressible through supported partial goals and may still require a manually designed FSM.
implementation: The character uses the neutral SMPL body with 69 degrees of freedom; the state space is 358-dimensional, and the action is a 69-dimensional PD target encoded with exponential maps. Current poses, velocities, future targets, and scene observations are canonicalized in the character's root-local frame, while root height is retained separately.

The first stage trains a fully constrained teacher with A2C: a Transformer actor consumes the current state, complete future full-body poses, and a local heightmap, while an MLP critic estimates value; the reward contains six terms for global joint position, rotation, root height, joint velocity, angular velocity, and energy. The training scene contains flat ground, irregular terrain, and an object playground, with early termination and prioritized motion sampling based on flat-ground failures.

The second stage freezes the teacher and lets the student control the simulation. Structured masking converts complete goals into partial goals; the prior consumes the current state, partial keyframes, pose history, XCLIP text, objects, and the heightmap, while the posterior additionally observes unmasked future poses; the decoder outputs PD actions from the current state, terrain, and latent. The teacher reads the complete goal at the same student-visited state to label actions, and training combines behavioral cloning of teacher actions with posterior-prior KL alignment.

The prior is a 4-layer, 4-head Transformer with model dimension 512, FFN dimension 1024, no dropout, and a 64-dimensional Gaussian latent; modality encoders are MLPs with hidden sizes [256, 256], while the posterior encoder and decoder use [1024, 1024, 1024] MLPs. Reparameterization noise epsilon is fixed within each episode during training; inference can use the prior mean for stable behavior or sample for diversity.

The student uses 11 future targets: the first 10 are consecutive near-term frames, and the 11th is a random long-term target; pose history consists of 5 poses sampled every 8 frames from the preceding 40 frames. Objects are represented by eight 3D bounding-box corners, a 6D orientation, and a category index; terrain uses a 16×16 heightmap with 10 cm spacing, and text uses a 512-dimensional XCLIP embedding.

Training aggregates AMASS, HumanML3D, and SAMP, with AMASS filtering, left-right mirroring, and random replacement of objects within the same class. The paper reports 16,384 parallel Isaac Gym environments on four A100 GPUs for approximately 14 days; the fully constrained teacher uses about 30 billion steps and MaskedMimic about 10 billion, with the policy running at 30 Hz and physics simulation at 120 Hz.

At deployment, the fully constrained teacher and privileged posterior are removed, leaving only the prior and decoder. Tasks such as path following, steering, reaching, and sitting are implemented by an external FSM that constructs or switches partial goals; thus task-specific retraining is eliminated, but task-specific goal, threshold, and state-machine engineering remains.

Quantitative results include 99.2% success and 35.1 mm MPJPE for full-body tracking on the AMASS test set; 98.1% success, 58.1 mm full-body MPJPE, and 45.8 mm observed-joint error for VR tracking; 95.4% and 93.6% success for full-body and VR tracking on irregular terrain; and 96.9% sitting success on held-out seating objects. Major quantitative evaluations use the prior mean, and the diversity-success tradeoff under random sampling is not quantified.

zh.title: M3imic: Learning a Versatile Whole-Body Controller for Multimodal Motion Mimicking
zh.authors: Zuxing Lu, Ziang Zheng, Yao Lyu, Jingyu Liu, Feihong Zhang, Song Lu, Xin Yuan, Changyin Sun, Xingxing Zuo, Shengbo Eben Li
zh.institutions: 东南大学自动化学院；清华大学车辆与运载学院；穆罕默德·本·扎耶德人工智能大学机器人学系
zh.takeaway: M3imic 最值得记住的是：它把机器人关节角、SMPL-X 人体姿态和稀疏末端位姿对齐到共享潜在命令空间，使同一个 Unitree G1 全身动作网络能够在密集参考的跟踪精度与稀疏参考的平衡鲁棒性之间切换，但核心潜空间损失缺少消融，控制接口与训练细节也不够完整。
zh.mainContent: 论文研究如何用一个低层全身控制器统一跟踪机器人关节角、SMPL-X 人体姿态和五个末端位姿三种结构与稀疏程度不同的运动参考。M3imic 使用模态专属编码器将短期参考窗口映射到 64 维共享潜在命令空间，并联合优化物理运动跟踪策略、模态内重建、潜变量对齐和机器人空间一致性损失。模型在 LAFAN1 与 100STYLE 上训练，在未见的 OMOMO 测试集上由末端模态取得 98.42% 的最高成功率，并在 Unitree G1 上完成零样本 Sim-to-Real 跟踪和光学动捕遥操作。该结果支持密集关节参考精度更高、稀疏末端参考更鲁棒的趋势，但论文没有直接量化 OOD 自编码器误差，也没有对三项核心潜空间损失逐项消融。
innovations: 为机器人关节角、SMPL-X 人体姿态和末端位姿分别设计编码器，将三种异构参考映射到连续的 64 维共享潜在命令空间，而不是先统一为显式关节轨迹或简单拼接带掩码的命令向量。
联合使用模态内重建损失、成对潜变量对齐损失，以及通过机器人解码器 D_r 计算的机器人空间一致性损失，使不同模态保留自身信息的同时具有共同的机器人控制语义。
将表示学习与物理运动跟踪强化学习组成单阶段训练框架，部署时只需选择对应模态编码器并复用同一个 Action Decoder，无需为每种输入模态重新训练策略；末端模式不需要部署时显式 IK，但训练数据仍依赖离线 GMR 重定向。
使用基于一秒动作片段终止失败率 EMA 的课程采样，在均匀采样与困难片段采样之间逐步过渡，并截断极端困难片段的采样概率。
系统性比较三种部署模态，观察到机器人关节参考具有更好的姿态和关节跟踪精度，而稀疏末端参考在动作分布变化下具有更高的成功率；主要贡献属于多模态表示与全身控制的系统整合，而非新的稳定性或收敛理论。
implementation: 数据预处理首先对人体动作进行筛选和 SMPL-X 整理，再通过 GMR 重定向到 29-DoF Unitree G1，形成时间对齐的机器人关节角、人体姿态和五个末端位姿三种参考。论文未说明具体筛选规则和 mini 数据子集的抽样方法。
机器人参考 q_t 为 29 维关节角；人体参考由 21 个关节的 6D rotation representation 构成；末端参考包含双手、双脚和胸部，每个末端由 3 维根坐标系相对位置和 6D 旋转表示构成。
每个控制时刻使用 H=10、采样间隔 Δ=2 的参考窗口，即索引 t、t+2 至 t+18。三个输入窗口分别为 10×29、10×21×6 和 10×5×9，并由模态专属 MLP 编码为 64 维潜变量。论文未说明控制周期，因此无法把该未来窗口换算为实际时间，也未解释在线遥操作如何取得未来参考。
三个模态解码器分别执行模态内重建；潜变量对齐损失最小化 z_r、z_h、z_e 的成对距离；一致性损失比较 D_r(z_r)、D_r(z_h) 和 D_r(z_e)，将机器人关节空间作为跨模态规范语义。
actor 输入潜在命令以及根姿态误差、基座角速度、实际关节角、关节速度和上一时刻动作；它刻意排除全局根位置与根线速度。critic 额外使用根位置误差、完整 body link 位置和姿态以及根线速度等仿真特权信息，部署时删除 critic。
总训练目标为策略损失与多模态自编码器损失之和。策略项采用 PPO 风格 clipped surrogate objective，包含 actor、value 和 entropy 项，实验部分称使用 RAD optimizer；论文未说明优势估计方法、clip 系数、学习率、损失权重及 RAD 与 clipped objective 的具体更新关系。
跟踪奖励包括根速度、根姿态、全身位置、全身姿态、全身线速度和全身角速度；正奖励权重依次为 0.5、0.5、1.0、1.0、1.0 和 1.0。正则项包括权重 -0.1 的动作变化、权重 -10.0 的关节越界和权重 -0.1 的碰撞惩罚；论文未给出各指数奖励的尺度参数。
课程学习将轨迹切分为一秒片段，以终止失败率 EMA 表示难度，并使用 P_final=αP_uniform+(1-α)clip(P_failure,0,P_max) 采样。消融实验设置 α_min=0.2、P_max=0.05；论文未给出 EMA 系数、α 调度曲线和截断后的概率归一化方法。
Sim-to-Real 训练随机化包括摩擦、外部推力、基座质心、基座质量、默认关节位置及姿态、角速度、关节位置和关节速度噪声。正文还提到 link mass、inertia、joint damping 和 motor strength，但表格没有给出相应范围。
训练数据为 LAFAN1 和 100STYLE，未见动作测试使用 OMOMO test subset。课程、数据规模和网络规模消融在 4 张 RTX 4090 上训练 50000 iterations；标准 MLP 配置为 512、256、128，大网络为 1024、512、256，但论文未报告主模型总训练时间和完整计算成本。
在训练数据上，M3imic 达到 99.54% 成功率、46.05 mm MPKPE、0.112 rad MPJAE 和 0.256 m/s 根速度误差。在 OMOMO 上，机器人参考模式的 MPKPE 和 MPJAE 最低，分别为 71.52 mm 和 0.139 rad；末端模式以 98.42% 获得最高成功率，但 MPKPE 和 MPJAE 略高。
真机光学动捕实验中，机器人参考模式与末端模式的 MPKPE 分别为 41.63 mm 和 43.22 mm，MPJAE 分别为 0.095 rad 和 0.105 rad。论文未报告试验次数、方差、真实成功率、端到端延迟、控制频率或推理硬件。
论文未说明动作 a_t 是关节位置目标、位置偏置还是力矩，也未给出动作维数、PD 增益、缩放和限幅。图 2 显示训练中的 Action Decoder 接收 z_r，而正文仅写未注明模态的 z_t，因此训练时是否让三种潜变量分别直接驱动 actor 仍不明确。

en.title: M3imic: Learning a Versatile Whole-Body Controller for Multimodal Motion Mimicking
en.authors: Zuxing Lu, Ziang Zheng, Yao Lyu, Jingyu Liu, Feihong Zhang, Song Lu, Xin Yuan, Changyin Sun, Xingxing Zuo, Shengbo Eben Li
en.institutions: School of Automation, Southeast University; School of Vehicle and Mobility, Tsinghua University; Department of Robotics, Mohamed Bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence
en.takeaway: The key idea to remember is that M3imic aligns robot joint angles, SMPL-X human poses, and sparse end-effector poses in a shared latent command space, allowing one Unitree G1 action network to trade dense-reference tracking fidelity for sparse-reference balance robustness, although the core latent losses are not ablated and important control and training details remain unspecified.
en.mainContent: The paper studies how a single low-level whole-body controller can track three motion-reference modalities with different structures and sparsity levels: robot joint angles, SMPL-X human poses, and five end-effector poses. M3imic uses modality-specific encoders to map short-horizon reference windows into a shared 64-dimensional latent command space and jointly optimizes physical motion tracking, within-modality reconstruction, latent alignment, and robot-space consistency. Trained on LAFAN1 and 100STYLE, the end-effector deployment mode reaches the highest success rate of 98.42% on the unseen OMOMO test set, and the controller is transferred zero-shot to Unitree G1 for tracking and optical-motion-capture teleoperation. The results support a fidelity-robustness trade-off between dense and sparse references, but the paper neither directly measures OOD autoencoder error nor ablates the three core latent-space losses.
innovations: It introduces separate encoders for robot joint angles, SMPL-X human poses, and end-effector poses, mapping the heterogeneous references into a continuous shared 64-dimensional latent command space instead of converting all commands into explicit joint trajectories or concatenating masked command vectors.

It combines within-modality reconstruction, pairwise latent alignment, and robot-space consistency through the robot decoder D_r so that each modality retains its own information while acquiring shared robot-control semantics.

It jointly trains representation learning and physics-based motion tracking in a single-stage framework. At deployment, a modality-specific encoder is paired with the same Action Decoder without modality-specific policy retraining; the end-effector mode avoids explicit runtime IK, although training data still depend on offline GMR retargeting.

It uses curriculum sampling based on an EMA of termination failure rates for one-second motion segments, gradually shifting from uniform sampling toward difficult segments while clipping extremely difficult cases.

It systematically compares the three deployment modalities and observes that robot-joint references provide better pose and joint tracking fidelity, whereas sparse end-effector references yield higher success under motion-distribution shift. The contribution is primarily a systems integration of multimodal representation learning and whole-body control rather than a new stability or convergence theory.
implementation: Human motion is filtered and processed in SMPL-X, then retargeted to the 29-DoF Unitree G1 with GMR to produce temporally aligned robot-joint, human-pose, and five-end-effector references. The paper does not specify the filtering criteria or how the mini data subset is sampled.

The robot reference q_t contains 29 joint angles. The human reference contains 21 joints represented with 6D rotations. The end-effector reference contains both hands, both feet, and the chest, with each pose represented by a 3D root-relative position and a 6D rotation.

At each control step, the encoders receive a reference horizon with H=10 and sampling interval Δ=2, covering indices t, t+2 through t+18. The three input sizes are 10×29, 10×21×6, and 10×5×9, and each modality-specific MLP produces a 64-dimensional latent code. The control period is not reported, so the physical duration of this future window and its causal handling in online teleoperation are unknown.

Three modality decoders perform within-modality reconstruction. The alignment loss minimizes pairwise distances among z_r, z_h, and z_e, while the consistency loss compares D_r(z_r), D_r(z_h), and D_r(z_e), using robot joint space as the canonical cross-modal semantics.

The actor receives the latent command, root-orientation error, base angular velocity, measured joint positions and velocities, and the previous action, while deliberately excluding global root position and root linear velocity. The critic additionally receives privileged simulation information including root-position error, full body-link positions and orientations, and root linear velocity, and is removed for deployment.

The total objective combines the policy loss and multimodal autoencoder loss. The policy term uses a PPO-style clipped surrogate objective with actor, value, and entropy components, and the experiments state that the model is optimized with RAD. The paper does not specify advantage estimation, clipping and learning-rate hyperparameters, loss coefficients, or how RAD is combined with the clipped objective.

Tracking rewards cover root velocity, root orientation, body position, body orientation, body linear velocity, and body angular velocity, with weights 0.5, 0.5, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, and 1.0. Regularization includes action-rate, joint-limit, and collision penalties with weights -0.1, -10.0, and -0.1, while the exponential reward scale parameters are not reported.

The curriculum divides trajectories into one-second segments, maintains an EMA of termination failure rate as difficulty, and samples with P_final=αP_uniform+(1-α)clip(P_failure,0,P_max). The ablation uses α_min=0.2 and P_max=0.05; the EMA coefficient, α schedule, and post-clipping normalization are not specified.

Sim-to-Real training randomizes friction, external pushes, base center of mass, base mass, default joint positions, and observation noise for orientation, angular velocity, joint position, and joint velocity. The text also mentions link mass, inertia, joint damping, and motor strength, but their ranges are absent from the table.

Training uses LAFAN1 and 100STYLE, with the OMOMO test subset used for unseen-motion evaluation. Curriculum, data-scale, and network-size ablations are trained for 50000 iterations on four RTX 4090 GPUs. The standard and large MLP configurations are 512-256-128 and 1024-512-256, but the main-model wall-clock training cost is not reported.

On the training datasets, M3imic reaches 99.54% success, 46.05 mm MPKPE, 0.112 rad MPJAE, and 0.256 m/s root-velocity error. On OMOMO, the robot-reference mode obtains the lowest M3imic MPKPE and MPJAE at 71.52 mm and 0.139 rad, while the end-effector mode achieves the highest success rate at 98.42% with slightly higher tracking errors.

In real-world optical-motion-capture experiments, the robot-reference and end-effector modes obtain MPKPE values of 41.63 mm and 43.22 mm and MPJAE values of 0.095 rad and 0.105 rad. The number of trials, variance, real-world success rate, end-to-end latency, control frequency, and inference hardware are not reported.

The paper does not specify whether action a_t is a joint-position target, position offset, or torque, and it omits the action dimension, PD gains, scaling, and limits. Figure 2 shows z_r entering the Action Decoder during training, whereas the text only refers to an unspecified z_t, leaving it unclear whether all three modality latents directly drive the actor during RL training.

zh.title: DynaRetarget: Dynamically-Feasible Retargeting using Sampling-Based Trajectory Optimization
zh.authors: Victor Dhédin, Ilyass Taouil, Shafeef Omar, Dian Yu, Kun Tao, Angela Dai, Majid Khadiv
zh.institutions: Munich Institute of Robotics and Machine Intelligence (MIRMI), Technical University of Munich (TUM), Germany
zh.takeaway: 把运动学重定向结果当作初值，在 MuJoCo 中用逐步扩展时域的 CEM/SBTO 搜索 PD-target，再用物理 rollout 训练 PPO tracker；核心创新是离线动力学精炼，而不是新的 IK 或 RL 算法。
zh.mainContent: DynaRetarget 面向接触丰富的人形 loco-manipulation，解决纯运动学重定向产生的缺失接触、穿透、脚滑和动力学不可执行问题。其核心 SBTO 在 MuJoCo 中用 CEM 优化稀疏 PD-target knots，逐步扩展优化时域，并允许早期控制变量在更长未来代价下继续更新；SBTO-skip 进一步缓存已收敛前缀。实验以 OmniRetarget 的 285 条 G1–箱子运动学轨迹为输入，SBTO-skip 的精炼成功率为 76.8%，高于 SPIDER 的 37.9%；使用精炼参考训练的 PPO tracker 在 8 条动作、1024 个 episode 上达到 97.09 ± 2.31% 成功率，而直接使用 OmniRetarget 参考为 79.41 ± 32.57%。论文还展示了策略零样本迁移至真机，但 SBTO 是离线过程：在 112 核 CPU 上精炼 1 秒动作约需 20 秒，且对低质量参考中的接触突变和物体姿态突翻仍会失败。
innovations: 据作者所知，提出首个在考虑完整问题时域的同时，将不完美运动学示范精炼为动力学可行人形 loco-manipulation 运动的采样式轨迹优化方法。
提出增量时域 SBTO：在当前窗口内反复执行 FHTO/CEM，协方差低于阈值后才加入下一个 knot；旧 knots 在更长有效时域下继续联合优化，从而预热最终 full-horizon 问题，并克服 SBMPC 的短视和已执行动作不可回溯问题。
提出 SBTO-skip：当前缀控制方差低于更严格阈值时，缓存其状态轨迹并跳过重复 rollout；Table III 中计算量由普通 SBTO 的 4.06e7 降至 1.18e7 个仿真步/秒参考动作，同时成功率由 74.6% 提升至 76.8%。
在系统层面将 IK 重定向、SBTO 动力学精炼和 PPO tracking 串联，并展示同一精炼目标可将单条示范适配到质量 0.1–8 kg、尺寸 0.2–0.4 m 的箱体以及圆柱、椅子和货架；下游 PPO 本身不是本文提出的新算法。
implementation: 系统概念管线为“人–物体示范 → IK-based retargeting → SBTO → PPO tracking → 零样本真机部署”。但评测并未重新提出或训练新的 IK 前端，而是直接读取 OmniRetarget 已生成的 285 条 G1–箱子运动学轨迹；官方仓库同样要求下载 OmniRetarget robot-object 数据。
SBTO 优化的是稀疏 PD-target knots，而不是直接改写仿真状态。初始化时先按 0.25 s 的 knot 间隔从输入的运动学参考关节序列中直接取样，得到一整组 reference knots，并把这组 knot 向量设为 CEM 初始高斯分布的均值，初始标准差为 0.25。因此这里的初值是运动学参考在低频 knot 参数化下的直接抽样，不是零值、随机轨迹或仿真状态。
初始化之后，每轮 CEM 都从当前多元高斯搜索分布中采样 N=1024 组完整的候选 knot 序列，而不是在每个时刻彼此独立地挑选单个 knot。每组候选 knots 经插值变成稠密 PD-target 序列，再使用完整机器人碰撞模型和 rollout API 在 MuJoCo 中并行执行；仿真步长为 0.01 s。
SBTO 代价同时跟踪关节、基座和物体的位置、姿态与速度，并加入 torso、foot、hand 的任务空间跟踪以及不期望的机器人–物体碰撞和自碰撞项。候选序列按当前有效窗口内的累计 rollout 代价排序，选择 elites 后更新下一轮 CEM 搜索分布。

从搜索分布的角度看，一轮 SBTO 就是“在参考 PD-target 附近随机探索 → 用 MuJoCo 检验每组候选产生的机器人–物体运动 → 提高低代价 elite 控制序列附近的采样概率”。CEM 根据 elites 的统计量并通过 EWMA 更新均值和完整协方差；经过多轮迭代，分布均值从原始运动学参考逐步迁移到代价更低、动力学更可行的 PD-target，协方差则在收缩搜索范围的同时编码不同关节与不同 knot 时刻之间的相关搜索方向。这是在优化当前轨迹实例的控制序列分布，不是在训练可泛化策略。
CEM 的 elite 比例为 0.03，使用完整协方差和 EWMA；均值与协方差 momentum 分别为 0.95 和 0.2，时域增长阈值为 0.055，前缀跳过阈值为 1e-4。论文没有给出 EWMA 的显式更新式，因此不能仅凭 momentum 数值判断其乘新统计量还是旧统计量。
在 285 条 OmniRetarget 轨迹上，SBTO-skip、普通 SBTO、SBTO-pos 和 SPIDER 的精炼成功率分别为 76.8%、74.6%、62.1% 和 37.9%。SBTO-skip 的归一化计算量为 1.18e7 个仿真步/秒参考动作；实际墙钟开销约为每精炼 1 秒动作需 20 秒，硬件为 112 核 Intel Xeon Platinum 8480+。
下游控制器采用 PPO 和 residual action space。策略观测包括一步期望机器人轨迹、一步物体位姿误差以及机器人坐标系中的物体位姿；奖励包括机器人全身与关节跟踪、物体位姿和速度跟踪、接触匹配、action rate、关节限位及自碰撞，其中接触项逐渐惩罚超过 10 N 的接触力。
PPO 在 mjlab（GPU 版 MuJoCo、IsaacLab 风格 API）中以 8192 个环境训练 10000 iterations，使用单张 RTX 4090。训练采用 adaptive sampling，并随机化物体初始位姿或速度、外力、摩擦和质量；作者没有加入物体跟踪失败终止条件。
训练好的策略通过 domain randomization 零样本迁移至真实人形机器人。论文未报告策略网络层数、控制频率、完整 PPO 训练墙钟时间或真机量化成功率；官方仓库明确开源的是 SBTO，不能据此认定完整 IK、PPO 和真机部署代码均已开源。

en.title: DynaRetarget: Dynamically-Feasible Retargeting using Sampling-Based Trajectory Optimization
en.authors: Victor Dhédin, Ilyass Taouil, Shafeef Omar, Dian Yu, Kun Tao, Angela Dai, Majid Khadiv
en.institutions: Munich Institute of Robotics and Machine Intelligence (MIRMI), Technical University of Munich (TUM), Germany
en.takeaway: Treat the kinematically retargeted motion as an initialization, use horizon-growing CEM/SBTO in MuJoCo to search for PD targets, and train a PPO tracker from the physical rollouts; the novelty is offline dynamic refinement rather than a new IK or RL algorithm.
en.mainContent: DynaRetarget targets contact-rich humanoid loco-manipulation and addresses missing contacts, penetrations, foot skating, and dynamic infeasibility left by purely kinematic retargeting. Its core SBTO method uses CEM in MuJoCo to optimize sparse PD-target knots, incrementally grows the optimization horizon, and keeps refining early controls under longer-term costs; SBTO-skip additionally caches converged prefixes. On 285 kinematically retargeted G1–box motions from OmniRetarget, SBTO-skip achieved a 76.8% refinement success rate versus 37.9% for SPIDER; PPO trackers trained from the refined references achieved 97.09 ± 2.31% success over 1024 episodes and 8 motions, compared with 79.41 ± 32.57% using OmniRetarget references directly. The paper also demonstrates zero-shot transfer to real hardware, but SBTO is an offline process: refining one second of motion takes roughly 20 seconds on a 112-core CPU, and poor references with abrupt contact changes or object-orientation flips remain failure cases.
innovations: To the authors' knowledge, this is the first sampling-based trajectory optimization method that refines imperfect kinematic demonstrations into dynamically feasible humanoid loco-manipulation motions while considering the full problem horizon.

The incremental-horizon SBTO repeatedly runs FHTO/CEM within the current window and adds a new knot only after covariance falls below a threshold; earlier knots remain jointly optimized under a longer effective horizon, warm-starting the final full-horizon problem and addressing SBMPC's myopia and irreversibility.

SBTO-skip caches a state prefix and skips repeated rollouts once the corresponding control variances fall below a stricter threshold. In Table III, it reduces compute from 4.06e7 to 1.18e7 simulation steps per second of reference motion while increasing success from 74.6% to 76.8%.

At the system level, the work connects IK retargeting, SBTO dynamic refinement, and PPO tracking, and shows that one demonstration can be adapted with the same objective to boxes of 0.1–8 kg and 0.2–0.4 m as well as a cylinder, chair, and shelf; the downstream PPO algorithm itself is not a new contribution.
implementation: The conceptual pipeline is human–object demonstration → IK-based retargeting → SBTO → PPO tracking → zero-shot real-robot deployment. The evaluation does not introduce or train a new IK front end; it directly consumes 285 kinematically retargeted G1–box trajectories from OmniRetarget, and the official repository likewise downloads the OmniRetarget robot-object data.

SBTO optimizes sparse PD-target knots rather than directly editing simulated states. At initialization, the input kinematic reference-joint sequence is sampled directly at the 0.25 s knot interval to form a complete set of reference knots, and this knot vector becomes the mean of the initial CEM Gaussian with a standard deviation of 0.25. The initialization is therefore a lower-frequency knot parameterization sampled from the kinematic reference, not a zero vector, random trajectory, or simulated state.

After initialization, every CEM iteration samples N=1024 complete candidate knot sequences from the current multivariate Gaussian search distribution rather than selecting each time-indexed knot independently. Each sampled knot sequence is interpolated into dense PD targets and executed in parallel through the MuJoCo rollout API with the full robot collision model and a 0.01 s simulation step.

The SBTO cost tracks joint, base, and object positions, orientations, and velocities, adds task-space tracking for the torso, feet, and hands, and penalizes undesired robot–object collisions and self-collisions. Candidate sequences are ranked by cumulative rollout cost over the current effective horizon; elites are then selected to update the next CEM search distribution.

Viewed as search-distribution optimization, one SBTO round is: randomly explore around the reference PD targets → use MuJoCo to evaluate the robot–object motion generated by each candidate → increase sampling probability around lower-cost elite control sequences. CEM updates the mean and full covariance from elite statistics through EWMA. Across iterations, the distribution mean moves from the original kinematic reference toward lower-cost, dynamically feasible PD targets, while the covariance contracts the search region and encodes correlated search directions across joints and knot times. This optimizes a control-sequence distribution for the current trajectory instance; it does not train a generalizable policy.

CEM uses an elite proportion of 0.03, a full covariance matrix, and EWMA. Mean and covariance momenta are 0.95 and 0.2, the horizon-increment threshold is 0.055, and the prefix-skip threshold is 1e-4. The paper does not provide the explicit EWMA update equation, so the momentum values alone do not establish whether they multiply new or old statistics.

Across 285 OmniRetarget motions, refinement success was 76.8% for SBTO-skip, 74.6% for SBTO, 62.1% for SBTO-pos, and 37.9% for SPIDER. SBTO-skip required 1.18e7 normalized simulation steps per second of reference motion; in wall-clock terms, refinement took about 20 seconds per second of motion on a 112-core Intel Xeon Platinum 8480+ CPU.

The downstream controller uses PPO with a residual action space. Observations include the one-step desired robot trajectory, one-step object-pose error, and object pose in the robot frame; rewards cover whole-body and joint tracking, object pose and velocity tracking, contact matching, action rate, joint limits, and self-collisions, with the contact term increasingly penalizing forces above 10 N.

PPO is trained in mjlab, a GPU MuJoCo environment with an IsaacLab-style API, using 8192 environments for 10000 iterations on one RTX 4090. Training uses adaptive sampling and randomizes object initial pose or velocity, external pushes, friction, and mass; the authors do not add object-tracking failure terminations.

The trained policy is transferred zero-shot to a real humanoid using domain randomization. The paper does not report the policy network architecture, control frequency, total PPO wall-clock training time, or quantitative real-robot success rates; the official repository explicitly releases SBTO, not necessarily the complete IK, PPO, and deployment stack.

zh.title: Kinodynamic Motion Retargeting for Humanoid Locomotion via Multi-Contact Whole-Body Trajectory Optimization
zh.authors: Xiaoyu Zhang, Steven Haener, Varun Madabushi, Maegan Tucker
zh.institutions: Georgia Institute of Technology, Atlanta, GA, USA
zh.takeaway: KDMR 将同步 MoCap marker 与 GRF 先解释为人体姿态和 heel/toe 接触日程，再用全身动力学 NLP 离线逐序列修正机器人参考轨迹；它的价值是生成更易被 BeyondMimic 跟踪策略学习的动力学可行数据，而不是提供可在线泛化的重定向模型。
zh.mainContent: 论文针对纯运动学 human-to-humanoid retargeting 容易产生脚底滑动、穿地、悬空和动力学不可行过渡的问题。方法先用 OpenSim 将光学 MoCap markers 拟合为人体姿态，从竖直 GRF 提取 heel-only、flat-foot 和 toe-only 接触阶段，再以差分 IK 生成 Unitree G1 的运动学参考，最后通过带浮动基刚体动力学、heel/toe 点接触、摩擦和驱动力限制的 NLP 联合修正当前优化时域内的轨迹与接触力。与 GMR 的选定跑步机步行片段对比显示，KDMR 的接触保持和轨迹平滑性更好；使用两类参考分别进行五次 BeyondMimic 训练时，KDMR 曲线表现出更快收敛。证据仍限于仿真和有限动作数据，论文没有消融、真机结果、NLP 求解时间或完整约束残差统计。
innovations: 核心创新：将 humanoid motion retargeting 表述为预给定 heel/toe 多接触日程下的全身动力学轨迹优化，在参考姿态跟踪之外显式加入浮动基刚体动力学、接触点驻留、摩擦和驱动力限制。
关键设计：利用同步 GRF 的竖直双峰形态识别 heel-only、flat-foot 与 toe-only 阶段，并将质量缩放后的单脚合力分解为 heel/toe 接触力变量，使优化能够表达自然的 heel-to-toe roll。
工程组合与验证：以 OpenSim 人体 IK、差分机器人 IK 和动力学 NLP 组成离线数据生成链，并用 BeyondMimic 下游策略训练比较说明动力学参考数据可能降低策略补偿非物理伪影的负担；OpenSim、CasADi、Pinocchio 和 BeyondMimic 本身均为继承组件。
implementation: 输入为同步的光学 marker 三维轨迹与测力板 GRF；OpenSim inverse kinematics 每个 keyframe 求人体骨架配置，再通过人体 forward kinematics 生成 hip、knee、ankle 等目标 frame 位姿。论文未给出 OpenSim 模型版本、marker 权重、完整 frame 列表或 human-to-robot link mapping。
接触预处理以竖直 GRF 的 mid-stance dip 为中心确定 flat-foot 窗口，其前后非零 GRF 时段分别标为 heel-only 和 toe-only；GRF 按 robot/human 质量比缩放，并满足单脚合力等于 heel 与 toe 力之和。该启发式针对 steady-state walking。
差分 IK 在速度层最小化机器人 frame 速度与人体目标 frame 速度的加权误差，并满足关节位置和速度边界，输出动力学阶段使用的参考/初始轨迹 \(\mathbf q^{\mathrm{ref}}\)。
动力学阶段在离散时域内联合优化机器人配置、速度、驱动力和四个 heel/toe 三维接触力；加速度是独立变量还是由离散关系导出，论文没有说明清楚。约束包括浮动基刚体动力学、stance 点零空间速度与加速度、正法向力、线性摩擦金字塔、关节/力矩边界和梯形积分；swing 点接触力设为零。
代价包含 base/reference tracking、leg joint tracking、相邻速度差、相邻 stance 接触力差、驱动力正则和 stance 点竖直高度软惩罚。论文给出 \(w_v=10^{-3}\)、\(w_\lambda=10^{-4}\)、\(w_\tau=10^{-4}\)、\(w_c=10^3\)，以及 base 和双腿关节的对角权重。
NLP 使用 CasADi 构造，Pinocchio 计算运动学和刚体动力学，目标机器人为 Unitree G1。论文没有说明具体 NLP backend、Hessian 处理、line search、容差、最大迭代数、warm start、分窗方式、边界条件或求解时间，因此该方法应视为每条新序列都需重新运行的离线逐实例求解器。
下游评估使用 BeyondMimic 默认超参数，KDMR 与 GMR 各进行五次训练，在相同迭代预算下只改变随机初始化种子；报告 mean reward 和 value function loss 的均值与标准差。论文没有真机部署、关键组件消融或多数据集泛化验证，代码仅声明将在正式发表时开源。
公式存在重要歧义：摘要所称 contact complementarity 在正文中实际表现为外部给定的二值接触日程与分模式约束，未展示标准 gap-force 互补条件；展示的 NLP 也未写出源 GRF tracking loss。论文称为梯形积分的两式使用相邻导数之差而非标准的和，不能确认是排版错误还是实际实现。

en.title: Kinodynamic Motion Retargeting for Humanoid Locomotion via Multi-Contact Whole-Body Trajectory Optimization
en.authors: Xiaoyu Zhang, Steven Haener, Varun Madabushi, Maegan Tucker
en.institutions: Georgia Institute of Technology, Atlanta, GA, USA
en.takeaway: KDMR converts synchronized MoCap markers and GRFs into human poses and a heel/toe contact schedule, then runs an offline whole-body dynamics NLP for every motion sequence; its value is producing dynamically feasible references that are easier for a BeyondMimic tracker to learn, not providing an online generalizable retargeting model.
en.mainContent: The paper addresses foot sliding, ground penetration or floating, and dynamically infeasible transitions introduced by purely kinematic human-to-humanoid retargeting. It fits optical MoCap markers to a human model with OpenSim, extracts heel-only, flat-foot, and toe-only phases from vertical GRF, generates a kinematic Unitree G1 reference with differential IK, and then jointly refines the trajectory and contact forces through an NLP with floating-base rigid-body dynamics, heel/toe point contacts, friction, and actuation limits. On a selected treadmill-walking segment, KDMR shows better contact preservation and smoother trajectories than GMR; five BeyondMimic runs per reference source show faster convergence with KDMR data. The evidence remains simulation-only and limited in motion coverage, with no ablation, hardware result, NLP runtime, or complete constraint-residual statistics.
innovations: Core novelty: formulate humanoid motion retargeting as whole-body dynamic trajectory optimization under a prescribed heel/toe multi-contact schedule, explicitly adding floating-base rigid-body dynamics, stationary contact-point conditions, friction, and actuation limits beyond pose tracking.

Key design: use the double-peaked vertical GRF profile to identify heel-only, flat-foot, and toe-only phases, and decompose the mass-scaled net foot force into heel and toe contact-force variables so that the optimizer can represent a natural heel-to-toe roll.

Engineering integration and validation: combine OpenSim human IK, differential robot IK, and a dynamics NLP into an offline data-generation pipeline, then use BeyondMimic training to test whether dynamically feasible references reduce the policy's burden of compensating for nonphysical artifacts; OpenSim, CasADi, Pinocchio, and BeyondMimic are inherited components rather than new algorithms.
implementation: Inputs are synchronized 3D optical-marker trajectories and force-plate GRFs. OpenSim inverse kinematics solves the human skeleton configuration at every keyframe, and human-model forward kinematics produces target-frame poses such as hip, knee, and ankle. The OpenSim model version, marker weights, complete frame list, and human-to-robot link mapping are not specified.

Contact preprocessing centers a flat-foot window around the mid-stance dip of the vertical GRF and labels the preceding and succeeding nonzero-GRF intervals as heel-only and toe-only. GRF is scaled by the robot-to-human mass ratio, with each foot's resultant represented as the sum of heel and toe forces. This heuristic is specific to steady-state walking.

Differential IK minimizes weighted task-space velocity errors between corresponding human and robot frames under joint-position and velocity bounds, producing the reference/initial trajectory \(\mathbf q^{\mathrm{ref}}\) for the dynamic stage.

The dynamic stage jointly optimizes robot configurations, velocities, actuation, and four 3D heel/toe contact forces over a discretized horizon; the paper is unclear whether acceleration is an independent variable or derived from the transcription. Constraints include floating-base rigid-body dynamics, zero spatial velocity and acceleration for stance points, positive normal force, a linearized friction pyramid, joint/torque bounds, and trapezoidal integration; swing contact forces are set to zero.

The objective includes base and leg-joint reference tracking, adjacent-velocity smoothing, adjacent stance-force smoothing, actuation regularization, and a soft vertical-height penalty on stance points. Reported weights include \(w_v=10^{-3}\), \(w_\lambda=10^{-4}\), \(w_\tau=10^{-4}\), and \(w_c=10^3\), together with diagonal base and bilateral leg-joint weights.

The NLP is formulated with CasADi and uses Pinocchio for kinematics and rigid-body dynamics, targeting the Unitree G1. The NLP backend, Hessian treatment, line search, tolerances, maximum iterations, warm start, windowing, boundary conditions, and solve time are not reported, so the method should be treated as an offline per-instance solver that must be rerun for each new sequence.

The downstream evaluation uses BeyondMimic default hyperparameters with five runs for KDMR and five for GMR, identical iteration budgets, and only random initialization seeds changed; mean reward and value-function loss are reported with mean and standard deviation. There is no hardware deployment, component ablation, or multi-dataset generalization test, and the paper only states that code will be released upon publication.

Important formulation ambiguities remain: the abstract's contact-complementarity claim is implemented in the shown equations as an externally prescribed binary contact schedule with mode-dependent constraints, not a standard gap-force complementarity condition; the displayed NLP also contains no explicit source-GRF tracking loss. The equations labeled as trapezoidal integration use differences rather than the standard sums of adjacent derivatives, so it is unclear whether this is a typographical error or the implemented form.

zh.title: MotionDisco: Motion Discovery for Extreme Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
zh.authors: Ilyass Taouil, Michal Ciebielski, Shafeef Omar, Haizhou Zhao, Angela Dai, Aaron M. Johnson, Majid Khadiv
zh.institutions: Technical University of Munich; New York University; Carnegie Mellon University
zh.takeaway: LLM 不直接生成逐帧动作，而是在离散接触方案空间中做进化搜索；顺序运动学优化与接触显式 TO 将候选方案变成连续参考轨迹，RL tracker 再负责鲁棒真机执行。
zh.mainContent: MotionDisco 面向无现成人类示范的长时域、富接触人形 loco-manipulation，目标是在不依赖遥操作或 human-to-humanoid motion retargeting 的情况下从零发现动作。给定完全已知的文本场景表示与任务目标，Claude Opus 4.7 在进化树中修改可执行的接触计划程序；顺序运动学优化先做廉价几何筛选，随后接触显式 TO 联合求解机器人—物体状态、控制、接触 wrench 与各接触阶段时长，并把数值和文本反馈返回搜索。论文在 8 个任务上报告完整方法均找到有效方案，且相较单次 LLM 调用以及无文本反馈的进化搜索获得更高的有效方案比例和更低的 TO cost；各任务首次有效解耗时为 1.34–7.49 分钟。发现的轨迹随后作为参考训练带 domain randomization 的 DeepMimic-style RL 跟踪策略并 zero-shot 部署到真机，但系统假设场景预先已知，且接触和物体模型受到明显限制。
innovations: 把长时域 loco-manipulation 表示成可执行程序形式的离散接触模式序列，并采用基于 ShinkaEvolve 的 LLM 引导进化树搜索；island 子群、inspiration sampling、novelty rejection 和多种 mutation 共同维持探索多样性。
设计分层 kinodynamic evaluator：先用忽略动力学的顺序运动学优化快速剔除几何不可行计划，再对通过者运行完整接触显式 TO；系统还定位最长可行前缀和首个失败接触转换，并将其转为文本反馈指导下一轮局部修补。
将自动接触方案发现、连续动力学轨迹生成和 RL 跟踪部署连成闭环。论文声称这是首个完全通过自动进化搜索发现并部署长时域人形 loco-manipulation 技能的工作，同时能够在一次搜索中产生多种不同的可行接触方案。
implementation: 搜索输入为场景 \(\mathcal{S}\) 与目标 \(\mathcal{G}\)：\(\mathcal{S}\) 是包含每个物体标签、世界位置和尺寸的已知文本场景，\(\mathcal{G}\) 可同时指定目标接触关系与机器人或物体的连续目标位姿。LLM 输出 Python 接触计划程序，程序执行后得到离散接触模式序列 \(\mathcal{C}\)，而不是输出 policy action 或逐帧轨迹。
每个搜索节点保存接触计划程序、执行得到的接触序列、标量 score、可选文本反馈和 offspring count。所有 LLM 组件使用 Claude Opus 4.7；mutation 类型为 targeted diff edit、full rewrite 和 crossover，采样概率分别为 0.6、0.3 和 0.1。
顺序运动学优化忽略动力学，仅检查碰撞规避、构型限制与接触转换一致性；若完整序列失败，程序反复缩短序列以找出最长可行前缀并报告首个失败 mode 或 transition。该阶段采用 direct multiple shooting transcription，并由 acados 求解。
对运动学可行的固定接触序列，TO 联合优化机器人—物体状态轨迹 \(x(\cdot)\)、控制轨迹 \(u(\cdot)\)、接触 wrench 以及各 mode 的持续时间 \(\bar{T}_{0:K-1}\)，同时约束动力学、接触、碰撞和状态/控制限位。TO 采用 direct multiple shooting transcription，并由 Hippo 求解。

TO 的抽象目标为 \(\int_0^T \phi(x(t),u(t))\,dt+\phi_T(x(T))+w_TT\)。用于评价接触方案的 cost 为 \(J(\mathcal{C})=\sum_i\lVert r(x_i,u_i,c_{s(i)})\rVert_1+w_j\sum_i\lVert\dddot q_i\rVert^2\)，即约束残差与 jerk 正则之和；运动学失败的节点不运行 TO，并获得零 score。论文未公开 \(\phi\)、\(\phi_T\) 的逐项构成、各代价权重、离散步长和完整停止条件。

评测包含 Banana、Box Stacking、Climb Table w/ Box、Long-Distance Pick & Place、Move Through Clutter、两项 Parkour Pick & Place 和 Under-Table Pick & Place 共 8 个任务。完整方法在全部任务中找到有效方案；论文把“通过顺序运动学检查且 TO 收敛”定义为 valid plan。

部署阶段将 TO 轨迹作为 reference，在仿真中用 DeepMimic-style rewards 和 domain randomization 训练 RL motion-tracking policy，再 zero-shot 迁移到真实人形机器人。论文未说明 policy 网络架构、具体 observation/action、RL 算法、奖励逐项公式、训练超参数、仿真器以及量化真机成功率，只报告所有尝试任务均实现多次连续成功执行。
关键限制是场景几何与初始状态必须预先已知且没有 perception；当前规划器只支持矩形 patch 上的 unilateral sticking contact，被操作对象限于 rigid box-like geometry，不支持滑动接触、关节物体、自由形状物体或软体。

en.title: MotionDisco: Motion Discovery for Extreme Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
en.authors: Ilyass Taouil, Michal Ciebielski, Shafeef Omar, Haizhou Zhao, Angela Dai, Aaron M. Johnson, Majid Khadiv
en.institutions: Technical University of Munich; New York University; Carnegie Mellon University
en.takeaway: The LLM does not generate frame-level actions: it evolves discrete contact plans, sequential kinematic optimization and contact-explicit TO turn them into continuous references, and an RL tracker provides robust hardware execution.
en.mainContent: MotionDisco targets long-horizon, contact-rich humanoid loco-manipulation without requiring teleoperation or human-to-humanoid motion retargeting. Given a fully known textual scene representation and task goal, Claude Opus 4.7 mutates executable contact-plan programs in an evolutionary tree; sequential kinematic optimization provides a cheap geometric filter, after which contact-explicit TO jointly solves robot-object states, controls, contact wrenches, and contact-stage durations while returning numerical and textual feedback to the search. Across eight tasks, the complete method found valid plans in every scenario and reported higher valid-plan rates and lower TO costs than a single LLM call and evolutionary search without textual feedback; time to the first valid solution ranged from 1.34 to 7.49 minutes. The discovered trajectories are then used as references for DeepMimic-style RL tracking with domain randomization and zero-shot hardware deployment, although the method assumes a known scene and uses restricted contact and object models.
innovations: It represents long-horizon loco-manipulation as executable programs over discrete contact-mode sequences and applies ShinkaEvolve-based LLM-guided evolutionary tree search, using island subpopulations, inspiration sampling, novelty rejection, and multiple mutation operators to preserve diversity.

It introduces a layered kinodynamic evaluator: dynamics-free sequential kinematic optimization first rejects geometrically infeasible plans, and full contact-explicit TO evaluates the survivors. The evaluator identifies the longest feasible prefix and first failing contact mode or transition, then converts this information into textual feedback for local repair in subsequent mutations.

It closes the loop from automated contact-plan discovery through continuous dynamically feasible trajectory generation to RL tracking on hardware. The paper claims the first deployment of long-horizon humanoid loco-manipulation skills discovered entirely through automated evolutionary search, while producing multiple distinct feasible solutions within a single run.
implementation: The search takes a scene \(\mathcal{S}\) and goal \(\mathcal{G}\). The known textual scene lists each object's label, world position, and dimensions, while the goal can include desired discrete contacts and continuous robot or object poses. The LLM outputs a Python contact-plan program whose execution produces a discrete mode sequence \(\mathcal{C}\), not policy actions or a frame-level trajectory.

Each tree node stores the contact-plan program, its executed contact sequence, a scalar score, optional textual feedback, and an offspring count. All LLM components use Claude Opus 4.7. The targeted-diff, full-rewrite, and crossover mutations are sampled with probabilities 0.6, 0.3, and 0.1, respectively.

Sequential kinematic optimization ignores dynamics and checks collision avoidance, configuration limits, and contact-transition consistency. When a full sequence fails, the system repeatedly shortens it to recover the longest feasible prefix and report the first failing mode or transition. This stage uses a direct multiple-shooting transcription solved with acados.

For a kinematically feasible fixed contact sequence, TO jointly optimizes the robot-object state trajectory \(x(\cdot)\), control trajectory \(u(\cdot)\), contact wrenches, and mode durations \(\bar{T}_{0:K-1}\), subject to dynamics, contact, collision, and state/control-limit constraints. The TO also uses direct multiple shooting and is solved with Hippo.

The abstract TO objective is \(\int_0^T \phi(x(t),u(t))\,dt+\phi_T(x(T))+w_TT\). Contact-plan evaluation uses \(J(\mathcal{C})=\sum_i\lVert r(x_i,u_i,c_{s(i)})\rVert_1+w_j\sum_i\lVert\dddot q_i\rVert^2\), combining constraint residuals and jerk regularization; a kinematically infeasible node skips TO and receives zero score. The paper does not disclose the full term-wise definitions of \(\phi\) and \(\phi_T\), all weights, discretization step, or complete stopping criteria.

Evaluation covers eight tasks: Banana, Box Stacking, Climb Table with Box, Long-Distance Pick and Place, Move Through Clutter, two Parkour Pick and Place variants, and Under-Table Pick and Place. The complete method found a valid plan for every task; a plan is considered valid when it passes sequential kinematic feasibility and TO converges.

For deployment, the TO trajectory becomes a reference for an RL motion-tracking policy trained in simulation with DeepMimic-style rewards and domain randomization, followed by zero-shot transfer to a real humanoid. The paper does not specify the policy architecture, exact observations/actions, RL algorithm, term-wise reward, training hyperparameters, simulator, or quantitative hardware success rate; it only reports multiple consecutive successful executions across all attempted tasks.

The method assumes known scene geometry and initial state and contains no perception. Its planner currently supports only unilateral sticking contacts on rectangular patches and rigid box-like manipulated objects, excluding sliding contact, articulated objects, free-form objects, and deformable objects.

zh.title: DeepLoco: Dynamic Locomotion Skills Using Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning
zh.authors: Xue Bin Peng, Glen Berseth, KangKang Yin, Michiel van de Panne
zh.institutions: University of British Columbia；National University of Singapore
zh.takeaway: DeepLoco 最该记住的不是一个从地图端到端输出力矩的单策略，而是一个顺序训练的两层控制系统：先训练并冻结能把“未来两步脚点与躯干朝向”转换为关节 PD target 的低层控制器，再为不同任务训练负责选择这些脚点的高层控制器，以具有物理语义的接口分开高频平衡控制和长期环境规划。
zh.mainContent: DeepLoco 研究模拟 3D 双足角色如何在保持自然、稳定行走的同时完成路径跟随、静态或动态避障和足球运球等环境感知任务。第一阶段利用手工动画或 mocap 片段构造模仿奖励，训练低层控制器从本体状态、固定步态相位和两步落脚计划输出 22 维关节 PD target；第二阶段冻结低层控制器，再让任务专用高层控制器从角色状态、局部环境地图和任务目标生成两步脚点与朝向。两层采用 CACLA 风格的正 TD actor–critic，而不是 PPO，也不是端到端联合训练。实验支持这种分阶段层级训练比作者构造的单层方案更容易优化，但全部结果来自简化角色和理想观测下的仿真，未验证真机部署、感知误差或 Sim-to-Real。
innovations: 核心创新：用“未来两步二维脚点＋下一步躯干朝向”作为高层与低层之间具有物理语义的接口，使高层只负责步级规划，低层只负责高频平衡、摆腿和落脚。
核心训练设计：先独立训练 LLC，再冻结 LLC 训练任务专用 HLC，避免联合训练时 LLC 持续变化导致高层所面对的等效动力学非平稳。层级强化学习本身并非本文首次提出，贡献主要在这一具体接口、训练顺序和完整系统。
系统贡献：同一个脚点接口同时支持路径跟随、静态与动态避障以及通过足部接触完成的足球运球，说明它可以作为多种环境感知 locomotion 任务的动作抽象。
关键辅助设计：用参考动作奖励降低三维双足行走的探索难度，并通过四槽双线性相位变换显式区分不同 gait phase；这些设计对训练很重要，但不是层级方法的核心创新。
有限的模块复用：不同风格 LLC 可由名义 LLC 微调得到，高层也可在更换 LLC 后继续微调；实验支持已有策略可作为有效初始化，但不支持 HLC 与 LLC 可以任意、无损地即插即用。
implementation: 数据准备：LLC 可以使用手工 keyframed walk cycle，也可以使用约 7 秒的 walking/turning mocap。后者被切成约 10 个单步片段，统一为右脚支撑并 time-warp 到 0.5 秒；训练时根据当前支撑腿镜像。最近邻选择器在每步开始时选取与目标脚点和朝向最匹配的参考片段。
LLC 输入输出：低层状态共 110 维，包含相对 root 表达的 link 位置、旋转、线速度和角速度、双足接触以及固定相位；另接收未来两步脚点和下一步躯干朝向。LLC 以 30 Hz 输出 22 维关节 PD target，而不是直接输出力矩。
参考动作的边界：参考片段只用于选择模仿目标和计算训练奖励，不作为 LLC 在线输入。运行时可以删除 mocap、参考片段选择器和模仿奖励，因此 LLC 不是 reference-conditioned tracker。
LLC 奖励：奖励由关节姿态、关节速度、root 高度、质心速度、摆动脚与支撑脚位置以及 heading 项组成。参考项维持动作风格，脚点和 heading 项让策略能够偏离参考并服从高层命令。
学习算法：两层均使用带最近 50k transitions 经验回放的 CACLA 式 actor–critic。critic 学习一步 bootstrap value；只有样本确实加入了探索噪声且 TD error 为正时，actor 才向该探索动作靠近。探索采用固定对角 Gaussian，并通过 Bernoulli 变量决定当前动作是否加入噪声；部署时只使用 actor 均值。
网络与优化：LLC actor 在四槽双线性相位变换后接 512、256 单元 ReLU 层并输出 22 维动作。优化器为带 0.9 momentum 的 SGD；actor 使用 0.0005 的 L2 weight decay，critic 不使用 weight decay。这是策略正则化的辅助技巧，不是核心贡献。
HLC 输入输出：静态环境任务的高层状态包含角色特征和角色中心坐标系下的 32×32 高度图，报告总维数为 1129；动态障碍任务改用记录障碍水平速度的 velocity map。HLC 还接收任务目标，并以 2 Hz 输出两个二维脚点和一个 heading，由接口定义可知共 5 维。
HLC 网络：地图依次经过 16 个 5×5、32 个 4×4、32 个 3×3 卷积滤波器和一个 128 单元全连接层，再与角色特征及任务目标拼接，经过 512、256 单元 ReLU 层输出脚点计划。论文未说明卷积 stride、padding、pooling 以及 HLC critic 的完整结构。
两阶段训练：名义 LLC 约训练 6M iterations；随后完全冻结 LLC，为路径、障碍或足球等每项任务分别训练一个 HLC，约 1M iterations。论文报告在 16 核 CPU 上 LLC 训练约 2 天、每个 HLC 约 7 天，但没有准确定义 iteration 对应 transition、batch 还是 SGD update。
运行闭环：HLC 每 0.5 秒生成一次落脚计划，LLC 在该计划下约执行 15 次更新；stable PD 将关节目标变成受限力矩，Bullet 以 3 kHz 推进物理仿真。运行时保留 HLC actor、LLC actor、固定相位、状态和地图提取、动作裁剪、PD 与物理系统；critic、replay buffer、reward、参考动作和探索噪声全部删除。
实验结论：Figure 11 中，分层版本在路径跟随和足球任务上明显优于作者的单层版本；Figure 8 表明多个参考片段能显著改善 LLC 学习。名义步态可承受论文所测的 200 N 前向推力、210 N 侧向推力和 16% 上坡，但实验没有多随机种子误差条、外部方法基线或真实机器人验证。
关键限制：系统依赖仿真真值本体状态、足接触、局部地图和球状态；默认 LLC 只会恒速行走与转向，不会停止，导致动态避障 NCR 仅为 0.18。每个新任务仍需训练新的 HLC，能力范围受 LLC skill repertoire 和脚点训练分布限制。
复现注意：Algorithm 1 的 critic target 与正文公式冲突，可能重复减去一次 value；双线性相位公式的最后一个槽也疑似把 Phi3 误印成重复的 Phi2。论文还缺少角色完整惯量与碰撞体、精确归一化参数、逐维探索方差、mocap 索引和 retarget 脚本等信息。

en.title: DeepLoco: Dynamic Locomotion Skills Using Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning
en.authors: Xue Bin Peng, Glen Berseth, KangKang Yin, Michiel van de Panne
en.institutions: University of British Columbia; National University of Singapore
en.takeaway: DeepLoco should be remembered not as a single end-to-end map-to-torque policy, but as a sequentially trained hierarchy: it first trains and freezes a low-level controller that converts a future two-step foot plan and torso heading into joint PD targets, and then trains task-specific high-level controllers to choose that semantic interface, separating high-frequency balance control from long-horizon environmental planning.
en.mainContent: DeepLoco studies how a simulated 3D biped can maintain natural, stable walking while performing environment-aware tasks such as path following, static or dynamic obstacle avoidance, and soccer dribbling. In the first stage, handcrafted animation or mocap clips define imitation rewards for an LLC that maps proprioceptive state, a fixed gait phase, and a two-step foot plan to 22-dimensional joint PD targets; in the second stage, the LLC is frozen and a task-specific HLC maps character state, a local environment map, and a task goal to two footsteps and a heading. Both levels use a positive-TD CACLA-style actor–critic rather than PPO, and they are not trained jointly end to end. The experiments support that this staged hierarchy is easier to optimize than the authors' monolithic alternative, but all results use a simplified simulated character with ideal observations and do not establish real-robot deployment, perception robustness, or Sim-to-Real transfer.
innovations: Core innovation: a physically meaningful interface consisting of two future 2D footsteps and a desired torso heading separates step-level planning in the HLC from high-frequency balance, swing-leg control, and landing in the LLC.

Core training design: the LLC is trained first and then frozen while task-specific HLCs are learned, avoiding the non-stationary effective dynamics faced by the HLC when the LLC changes during joint training. Hierarchical RL itself was not introduced by this paper; the contribution lies in this concrete interface, training order, and complete system.

System contribution: the same footstep interface supports path following, static and dynamic obstacle avoidance, and soccer dribbling through foot–ball contact, demonstrating its value as an action abstraction for multiple environment-aware locomotion tasks.

Key auxiliary design: reference-motion rewards reduce the exploration burden of 3D bipedal walking, while a four-slot bilinear phase transform explicitly separates gait phases. These components are important to training but are not the central hierarchical contribution.

Limited module reuse: style-specific LLCs are fine-tuned from a nominal LLC, and HLCs can be fine-tuned after changing the LLC. The evidence supports reuse as a useful initialization, not arbitrary lossless plug-and-play compatibility.
implementation: Data preparation: the LLC can use either a handcrafted keyframed walk cycle or roughly seven seconds of walking and turning mocap. The mocap is divided into about ten single-step clips, normalized to right-foot support, and time-warped to 0.5 seconds; clips are mirrored according to the current support leg. At each step, a nearest-neighbor selector chooses the clip best matching the requested foot placement and heading.

LLC inputs and outputs: the 110-dimensional low-level state contains root-relative link positions, rotations, linear and angular velocities, two foot-contact indicators, and a fixed phase. It also receives two future footsteps and a desired torso heading. At 30 Hz, the LLC outputs 22-dimensional joint PD targets rather than torques.

Boundary of reference motion: reference clips are used only to select imitation targets and compute training rewards; they are not LLC runtime inputs. Mocap, the reference selector, and imitation rewards can therefore be removed at runtime, so the LLC is not a reference-conditioned tracker.

LLC reward: the objective combines joint-pose, joint-velocity, root-height, center-of-mass velocity, swing- and stance-foot position, and heading terms. Reference terms preserve motion style, while foot-placement and heading terms allow the policy to deviate from the reference and follow high-level commands.

Learning algorithm: both levels use a CACLA-style actor–critic with a replay buffer containing the latest 50k transitions. The critic learns a one-step bootstrapped value; the actor moves toward an exploratory action only when noise was actually applied and the TD error is positive. Exploration uses a fixed diagonal Gaussian gated by a Bernoulli variable, while runtime execution uses only the actor mean.

Network and optimization: after the four-slot bilinear phase transform, the LLC actor uses 512- and 256-unit ReLU layers and a 22-dimensional output. Optimization uses SGD with 0.9 momentum; the actor has L2 weight decay of 0.0005, while the critic has no weight decay. This is an auxiliary policy-regularization choice rather than a core contribution.

HLC inputs and outputs: for static-environment tasks, the high-level state combines character features with a character-centric 32×32 height map and is reported as 1129-dimensional; dynamic-obstacle tasks replace it with a velocity map encoding horizontal obstacle velocities. The HLC additionally receives a task goal and outputs two 2D footsteps plus one heading at 2 Hz, yielding a five-dimensional interface by construction.

HLC network: the map passes through 16 filters of size 5×5, 32 filters of size 4×4, 32 filters of size 3×3, and a 128-unit fully connected layer. The result is concatenated with character features and the task goal, followed by 512- and 256-unit ReLU layers. Convolution stride, padding, pooling, and the complete HLC critic architecture are not specified.

Two-stage training: the nominal LLC is trained for about 6M iterations and then fully frozen; a separate HLC is trained for each path, obstacle, or soccer task for about 1M iterations. The paper reports roughly two days for LLC training and seven days per HLC on a 16-core CPU, but it does not define whether an iteration denotes a transition, batch, or SGD update.

Runtime loop: the HLC generates a foot plan every 0.5 seconds, during which the LLC performs about 15 updates. Stable PD converts joint targets into bounded torques, and Bullet advances physics at 3 kHz. Runtime retains the HLC actor, LLC actor, fixed phase, state and map extraction, action clipping, PD, and physical system; critics, replay buffers, rewards, reference motions, and exploration noise are removed.

Experimental conclusion: Figure 11 shows that the hierarchical version substantially outperforms the authors' monolithic versions on path following and soccer, while Figure 8 shows that multiple reference clips improve LLC learning. The nominal gait tolerates the tested 200 N forward push, 210 N lateral push, and 16% uphill slope, but the experiments provide no multi-seed error bars, external-method baseline, or real-robot validation.

Key limitations: the system relies on simulation-ground-truth proprioception, foot contacts, local maps, and ball state. The default LLC only walks and turns at an approximately fixed speed and cannot stop, contributing to the low dynamic-obstacle NCR of 0.18. Each new heterogeneous task still requires a new HLC, and the system is bounded by the LLC skill repertoire and footstep-training distribution.

Reproduction caveats: the critic target in Algorithm 1 conflicts with the main-text equations and may subtract the value twice; the final slot in the bilinear phase equation also appears to repeat Phi2 instead of Phi3. Complete link inertias and collision geometry, precise normalization parameters, per-dimension exploration variances, mocap indices, and retargeting scripts are also missing.

zh.title: Retargeting Matters: General Motion Retargeting for Humanoid Motion Tracking
zh.authors: João Pedro Araújo, Yanjie Ze, Pei Xu, Jiajun Wu, C. Karen Liu
zh.institutions: Department of Computer Science, School of Engineering, Stanford University
zh.takeaway: GMR 最该记住的是：它不是训练得到的重定向网络，而是用“局部非均匀缩放 + 两阶段逐帧 IK”把每条人体动作转换成机器人参考轨迹的逐实例运动学求解器；固定 BeyondMimic 管线的实验进一步表明，重定向产生的穿地、自交和关节突跳会直接削弱下游物理跟踪策略的鲁棒性。
zh.mainContent: 人体与人形机器人在骨长、关节拓扑和活动范围上的差异，会让传统重定向产生足滑、穿地、自交或关节突跳，而这些 reference artifact 会被下游 RL tracker 直接继承。GMR 接收人体骨架动作、机器人 XML/URDF 和人工适配配置，通过 rest-pose 对齐、root 全局运动与 body 局部形态的解耦缩放，以及两阶段逐帧 IK，输出机器人 root 位姿与关节轨迹。作者在 Unitree G1 上使用 LAFAN1 的 21 条动作和统一的 BeyondMimic 训练管线，对比 PHC、ProtoMotions、GMR 与闭源 Unitree reference；GMR 总体上优于两个开源基线，并在成功率、跟踪误差和感知忠实度上接近 Unitree。结论仍限于运动学重定向及仿真/sim2sim 评估：论文没有真机、跨机器人、复杂接触或组件消融，也未证明 GMR 输出本身满足动力学可行性。
innovations: 核心方法创新是局部非均匀缩放：body 相对 root 的位置可使用不同局部比例，而 root 的世界坐标平移始终使用统一比例，从而把“机器人整体应移动多远”与“各肢体相对骨盆应伸展多远”解耦，并针对传统缩放造成的形变和足滑问题进行处理。
将上述缩放与两阶段 IK 组合成完整重定向流程：第一阶段跟踪全部关键体旋转和手脚位置，意在先获得较合理的粗构型与 IK 解支；第二阶段以其结果为初值，再加入全部关键体的位置约束进行精修。论文没有单阶段对照或组件消融，因此不能确认两阶段设计的独立增益。
实验性贡献是把 retargeting quality 放入固定物理跟踪管线中进行端到端评估：作者不针对不同 retargeter 重新调节 BeyondMimic 奖励，并结合 sim、sim-dr、sim2sim、跟踪误差与用户研究分析 reference artifact 和首帧选择对策略学习及鲁棒性的影响。这属于评估设计贡献，而不是新的 RL 算法。
implementation: GMR 的输入包括人体 skeleton pose、机器人 XML/URDF，以及人工设置的关键体映射、位置/旋转权重、rest-pose offset、局部 scale 和 joint limits；实验中的人体输入为 LAFAN1 BVH。输出是逐帧机器人广义坐标序列，包括 root translation、root rotation 和 joint values，它是下游 tracking policy 的 reference，而不是控制 action。
预处理先对齐人体与机器人关键体在 rest pose 下的坐标轴，并可为个别 body 添加位置 offset；随后分别缩放 body 相对 root 的局部位置与 root 的全局平移。论文没有给出各 scale、offset、权重的自动学习规则或完整 G1 配置，这些量属于人工适配参数。
每帧第一阶段直接优化机器人姿态：目标包含全部映射关键体的旋转误差，以及手、脚的 Cartesian 位置误差，并受 joint limits 约束。第一帧使用缩放后的人体 root position 和 root yaw 初始化；其余关节以及 root roll/pitch 的初值论文未说明。
第一阶段使用 Mink differential IK：在当前姿态附近线性化残差，求能够降低误差的广义速度，再积分更新姿态。求解在目标值变化低于 0.001 时停止，或者最多运行 10 次迭代。
第二阶段以第一阶段结果为初值，保留关键体旋转目标，并把位置目标从手脚扩展到全部关键体，使用另一组权重继续求解；终止条件与第一阶段相同。论文没有在 Step 5 再次明确 solver，结合上下文可推测仍使用 Mink，但这不是正文明确确认的实现细节。
动作序列按时间顺序逐帧求解，从第二帧开始以上一帧结果作为 Step 4 的 warm start。整段完成后，通过 FK 计算机器人各 body 的高度，并对 root translation 施加统一竖直偏移以修正整体悬空或穿地；该流程不是含速度、加速度和接触时序的整段 trajectory optimization。
GMR 本身没有神经网络参数，也不进行监督学习或强化学习；每条新动作都需要重新运行逐帧 IK。相同人体骨架约定与机器人组合的映射和配置原则上可以复用，但论文未完整说明其缓存与自动适配策略。
下游评估阶段为每条 retargeted reference 单独训练 BeyondMimic single-trajectory policy。每个策略分别进行 100 次 sim、4096 次 sim-dr 和 100 次 sim2sim rollout；sim2sim 使用 BeyondMimic 的 ROS 状态估计与推理包在 MuJoCo 中运行，不是真机实验。
在本文固定 reference 的评估流程中，GMR 只负责离线生成参考轨迹，随后 RL 训练和 sim2sim 推理不再更新或调用 GMR。论文没有报告 GMR 在线运行频率，也没有给出 BeyondMimic 的 observation、action、actor/critic、reward、控制频率、PD 参数、训练预算或 seed，因此这些细节不能从本文补写。
公开目标只包含运动学位置、旋转和 joint-limit 约束，没有接触状态、足端零速度、碰撞、摩擦、力矩、速度、加速度或显式平滑项；因此输出是较易跟踪的运动学 reference，而不是由 GMR 保证动力学可执行的控制轨迹。

en.title: Retargeting Matters: General Motion Retargeting for Humanoid Motion Tracking
en.authors: João Pedro Araújo, Yanjie Ze, Pei Xu, Jiajun Wu, C. Karen Liu
en.institutions: Department of Computer Science, School of Engineering, Stanford University
en.takeaway: GMR should be remembered not as a learned retargeting network, but as a per-instance kinematic solver that converts each human motion into a robot reference trajectory through non-uniform local scaling and two-stage framewise IK; experiments with a fixed BeyondMimic pipeline further show that ground penetration, self-intersection, and joint discontinuities introduced during retargeting can directly reduce downstream physical tracking robustness.
en.mainContent: Differences in bone lengths, joint topology, and range of motion between humans and humanoids can make conventional retargeting produce foot sliding, ground penetration, self-intersection, or abrupt joint changes, which are then inherited by downstream RL trackers. GMR takes human skeletal motion, a robot XML/URDF model, and manually specified adaptation parameters, then applies rest-pose alignment, decoupled scaling of global root motion and local body shape, and two-stage framewise IK to output robot root poses and joint trajectories. On 21 LAFAN1 motions retargeted to the Unitree G1 and evaluated with a fixed BeyondMimic training pipeline, GMR generally outperforms the two open-source baselines, PHC and ProtoMotions, and approaches the closed-source Unitree references in success rate, tracking error, and perceptual fidelity. The evidence remains limited to kinematic retargeting and simulation/sim2sim evaluation: the paper provides no real-robot, cross-robot, complex-contact, or component-ablation experiments and does not establish that GMR outputs are dynamically feasible by themselves.
innovations: The core method contribution is non-uniform local scaling: body positions relative to the root may use body-specific scale factors, while the root translation in world coordinates always uses one uniform factor. This separates how far the robot should travel globally from how far individual limbs should extend relative to the pelvis, targeting deformation and foot-sliding artifacts caused by conventional scaling.

The scaling procedure is combined with a two-stage IK pipeline. Stage 1 tracks all mapped body orientations and the Cartesian positions of the hands and feet, with the intent of first finding a more plausible coarse configuration and IK branch; Stage 2 uses that solution as initialization and adds position constraints for all key bodies. The paper provides neither a single-stage comparison nor a component ablation, so the independent gain of the two-stage design is not established.

The experimental contribution is an end-to-end evaluation of retargeting quality inside a fixed physical tracking pipeline. BeyondMimic rewards are not retuned for different retargeters, and sim, sim-dr, sim2sim, tracking-error, and user-study evidence is combined to examine how reference artifacts and initial-frame selection affect learning and robustness. This is an evaluation contribution rather than a new RL algorithm.
implementation: GMR takes a human skeleton pose, a robot XML/URDF model, and manually specified key-body mappings, position/orientation weights, rest-pose offsets, local scales, and joint limits. The experiments use LAFAN1 BVH motions. Its output is a sequence of robot generalized coordinates containing root translation, root rotation, and joint values; this sequence is a reference for a downstream tracking policy, not a control action.

Preprocessing first aligns the coordinate frames of corresponding human and robot bodies in their rest poses and may add position offsets to selected bodies. It then scales body positions relative to the root separately from the global root translation. The paper does not provide an automatic learning rule or the complete G1 values for all scales, offsets, and weights; they are adaptation parameters.

For each frame, Stage 1 directly optimizes the robot configuration using orientation errors for all mapped key bodies and Cartesian position errors for the hands and feet, subject to joint limits. The first frame initializes the root from the scaled human root position and root yaw; the initial values of the remaining joints and root roll/pitch are not specified.

Stage 1 uses Mink differential IK: it linearizes the residual around the current configuration, solves for generalized velocities that reduce the error, and integrates them to update the pose. It stops when the objective change is below 0.001 or after at most 10 iterations.

Stage 2 starts from the Stage 1 solution, retains key-body orientation targets, and expands position tracking from the hands and feet to all key bodies using a second set of weights. The same termination conditions apply. Because the paper does not explicitly restate the solver used in Step 5, Mink remains the context-supported interpretation rather than an explicitly confirmed implementation detail.

Motion sequences are solved sequentially, with each frame after the first warm-started from the previous solution in Step 4. After the sequence is processed, FK is used to compute robot-body heights and a uniform vertical offset is applied to the root translation to correct global floating or ground penetration. This is not a joint trajectory optimization with velocity, acceleration, or contact-timing terms.

GMR has no neural-network parameters and performs neither supervised nor reinforcement learning; each new motion clip must be solved again with framewise IK. Mappings and configuration parameters can in principle be reused for the same human-skeleton convention and robot, but the paper does not fully specify caching or automatic adaptation.

For downstream evaluation, a separate BeyondMimic single-trajectory policy is trained for each retargeted reference. Each policy is evaluated with 100 sim, 4096 sim-dr, and 100 sim2sim rollouts. Sim2sim runs the BeyondMimic ROS state-estimation and inference package with MuJoCo and is not a real-robot experiment.

In the paper's fixed-reference evaluation pipeline, GMR is used only to generate references offline; subsequent RL training and sim2sim inference neither update nor call GMR. The paper does not report an online GMR frequency or specify BeyondMimic observations, actions, actor/critic networks, rewards, control rate, PD parameters, training budget, or seeds, so those details should not be filled in from this paper.

The published objective contains only kinematic position, orientation, and joint-limit constraints. It includes no contact state, zero foot-velocity constraint, collision, friction, torque, velocity, acceleration, or explicit smoothing term. The output is therefore a kinematic reference intended to be easier to track, not a control trajectory whose dynamic feasibility is guaranteed by GMR.

zh.title: Physics-Based Motion Imitation with Adversarial Differential Discriminators
zh.authors: Ziyu Zhang, Sergey Bashkirov, Dun Yang, Yi Shi, Michael Taylor, Xue Bin Peng
zh.institutions: Simon Fraser University; Sony PlayStation; NVIDIA
zh.takeaway: ADD 不是动作生成器，而是训练期的可学习 reward 聚合器：它保留 reference-conditioned mimic 的逐帧跟踪与 PPO/PD 控制链，只把手工加权的多项 tracking reward 换成判别器输出；因此真正有意义的基线是 DeepMimic，AMP 只能作为不同模仿目标的参照。
zh.mainContent: 论文解决物理角色逐帧跟踪中姿态、位置与速度等多项目标需要人工定权的问题。给定同步参考状态与仿真状态，方法构造差分向量 \(\boldsymbol{\Delta}_t=\phi(\hat{\mathbf{s}}_t)\ominus\phi(\mathbf{s}_t)\)，以零向量作为判别器唯一正样本、策略 rollout 产生的差分作为负类样本，再将判别分数变成 PPO 的标量奖励；actor 仍输出关节目标旋转并由 PD 执行。13 个单动作、DanceDB 与 LaFAN1 子集实验表明 ADD 在多数任务上达到或超过 DeepMimic，并能扩展到 Walker、Go1 等非模仿多目标任务，但 Run、Sideflip、Roll 等任务暴露了 root 误差被高维特征稀释和局部最优问题。论文没有真机实验；AMP 对比只能说明同步逐帧误差更适合 precise tracking，不能证明 ADD 是更好的通用 imitation 方法。
innovations: 核心创新：提出 Adversarial Differential Discriminator（ADD），用 MLP 判别器替代多目标损失的固定线性加权，将高维差分非线性地聚合为单一训练信号，并允许聚合关系随当前策略误差分布变化。
核心机制：把理想解统一表示为唯一的零差分正样本，把当前模型或策略产生的差分作为负类样本；判别器学习的是“当前误差离理想零点有多近”，而不是 AMP 式 expert motion distribution。
关键辅助设计：在策略实际产生的负类差分附近施加 zero-centered gradient penalty，避免判别器退化为只识别精确零点的硬分类器；消融显示没有该项或直接采用 WGAN-GP 时多数任务失败。
工程扩展：同一 ADD 聚合形式被用于精确 motion tracking、imitation + steering，以及 Walker/Go1 的非模仿多目标 RL；reference-conditioned actor、PPO、GAE、TD(λ) 与 PD controller 均属于继承组件，不是本文新提出的控制接口。
implementation: 输入与差分：参考状态和同一时刻的仿真状态先映射为同构特征，再计算 \(\boldsymbol{\Delta}_t\)。差分包含 root 全局位置/旋转、各关节局部位置与全局旋转、root 局部线/角速度及各关节局部速度；论文没有逐项说明 \(\ominus\) 对旋转的精确实现，也未完整给出不同量纲特征的归一化方式。
Actor 接收当前各 body link 相对 root 的位置、6D normal-tangent 旋转、局部线/角速度以及同步目标 reference pose，输出高斯动作分布下的关节目标旋转；球关节使用 3D exponential map，转动关节输出标量角度，随后由 PD controller 转成执行力矩。

训练循环：策略在 Isaac Gym 中 rollout，逐步计算差分与奖励 \(r_t=-\log(1-D(\boldsymbol{\Delta}_t))\)；GAE 估计优势、TD(λ) 构造 value target，PPO 更新 actor，回归损失更新 critic，判别器使用零向量正类与 rollout/cache 中的差分负类交替更新。判别器梯度不会穿过仿真器直接回传给 actor。
网络与优化：actor、critic 和 discriminator 都使用 1024、512 单元的两层 ReLU MLP；actor 后接线性动作头，critic 与 discriminator 输出标量。策略协方差是人工指定的固定对角阵；论文未报告 asymmetric privileged critic、历史堆叠或明确的未来参考窗口。

控制与训练规模：28-DoF humanoid 的仿真/策略频率为 120/30 Hz，26-DoF Sony EVAL 为 150/50 Hz；主要实验使用 NVIDIA A100。多数单动作约训练 7.5–8.5 亿 samples，ADD 约 9 h；DanceDB 约 90 亿 samples、约 5 天，LaFAN1 子集约 180 亿 samples、约 10 天，因此它减少的是 reward 调参成本而不是计算成本。
关键证据与失败：Double Kong 的位置误差为 ADD 0.030 m、DeepMimic 0.223 m；DanceDB 为 0.044/0.045 m，LaFAN1 为 0.028/0.029 m。Run 上 ADD 为 0.165 m、DeepMimic 为 0.013 m，且 Sideflip、Roll 会出现局部最优，说明判别器自动聚合不保证学到任务上最重要的权衡。

训练/部署边界：训练时需要参考动作、物理仿真器、ADD、critic、PPO/GAE、经验缓存和梯度惩罚；推理时只保留当前状态、同步 reference pose、冻结 actor 与 PD controller，ADD 和 tracking 差分都不再运行。论文全部结果均为仿真，没有 system identification、domain randomization、延迟/噪声建模或真机部署证据。

对比边界：ADD 与 DeepMimic 都是逐帧 reference-conditioned tracker，主要区别是 reward scalarization；AMP 判别 expert 与 policy 的状态转移分布，不要求与指定参考帧同步。用逐帧 tracking error 比较 AMP 天然偏向 ADD/DeepMimic，因此 AMP 结果不能支持“ADD 是更强的通用 adversarial imitation”这一结论。

en.title: Physics-Based Motion Imitation with Adversarial Differential Discriminators
en.authors: Ziyu Zhang, Sergey Bashkirov, Dun Yang, Yi Shi, Michael Taylor, Xue Bin Peng
en.institutions: Simon Fraser University; Sony PlayStation; NVIDIA
en.takeaway: ADD is not a motion generator but a learned training-time reward aggregator: it keeps the reference-conditioned frame-tracking and PPO/PD control pipeline while replacing the manually weighted tracking reward with a discriminator output; DeepMimic is therefore the substantive baseline, whereas AMP serves only as a reference with a different imitation objective.
en.mainContent: The paper addresses the manual weighting of pose, position, and velocity objectives in frame-synchronous physics-based motion tracking. Given aligned reference and simulated states, it constructs a differential vector \(\boldsymbol{\Delta}_t=\phi(\hat{\mathbf{s}}_t)\ominus\phi(\mathbf{s}_t)\), uses the zero vector as the discriminator's sole positive sample and rollout differentials as negative-class samples, and converts the score into a scalar PPO reward; the actor still outputs joint target rotations executed by a PD controller. Experiments on 13 individual motions, DanceDB, and a LaFAN1 subset show that ADD matches or exceeds DeepMimic on most tasks and extends to non-imitation Walker and Go1 multi-objective tasks, while Run, Sideflip, and Roll expose root-error dilution and local optima. The paper reports no real-robot experiments; its AMP comparison shows that synchronized per-frame errors are better suited to precise tracking than unsynchronized distribution matching, not that ADD is a universally superior imitation method.
innovations: Core innovation: Adversarial Differential Discriminator (ADD) replaces a fixed weighted sum of objectives with an MLP discriminator that nonlinearly aggregates a high-dimensional differential into one training signal and can adapt to the current error distribution.

Core mechanism: the ideal solution is represented by a single zero-differential positive sample, while differentials produced by the current model or policy form the negative class; unlike AMP, the discriminator learns proximity to an ideal zero-error point rather than an expert motion distribution.

Key supporting design: a zero-centered gradient penalty is applied near policy-generated negative-class differentials to prevent the discriminator from becoming a hard detector of the exact zero point; the ablation shows that omitting it or directly using WGAN-GP causes most tasks to fail.

Engineering extension: the same ADD aggregation is applied to precise motion tracking, imitation plus steering, and non-imitation Walker/Go1 multi-objective RL. The reference-conditioned actor, PPO, GAE, TD(λ), and PD controller are inherited components rather than new control interfaces introduced by this paper.
implementation: Inputs and differential: aligned reference and simulated states are mapped to matching features before computing \(\boldsymbol{\Delta}_t\). Features include global root position/rotation, local joint positions and global joint rotations, local root linear/angular velocities, and local joint velocities; the paper does not specify the exact rotational implementation of \(\ominus\) or the complete normalization across units.

The actor receives current body-link positions relative to the root, 6D normal-tangent rotations, local linear/angular velocities, and a synchronized target reference pose. It outputs Gaussian-distributed joint target rotations: 3D exponential maps for spherical joints and scalar angles for revolute joints, followed by a PD controller that produces torques.

Training loop: the policy rolls out in Isaac Gym and computes \(r_t=-\log(1-D(\boldsymbol{\Delta}_t))\) at every step. GAE estimates advantages, TD(λ) supplies value targets, PPO updates the actor, regression updates the critic, and the discriminator alternates updates using zero-vector positives and rollout/cache differential negatives. Discriminator gradients are not backpropagated through the simulator into the actor.

Networks and optimization: actor, critic, and discriminator use two-layer ReLU MLPs with 1024 and 512 hidden units. The actor has a linear action head, while critic and discriminator output scalars. The policy covariance is a manually specified fixed diagonal matrix; the paper does not report an asymmetric privileged critic, observation history stacking, or a clearly defined future reference window.

Control and training scale: the 28-DoF humanoid runs at 120 Hz simulation and 30 Hz policy frequency, while the 26-DoF Sony EVAL runs at 150/50 Hz; major experiments use an NVIDIA A100. Most single-motion runs use roughly 0.75–0.85 billion samples and about 9 h for ADD; DanceDB uses about 9 billion samples and 5 days, and the LaFAN1 subset about 18 billion samples and 10 days, so the method reduces reward-tuning effort rather than computation.

Key evidence and failures: Double Kong position error is 0.030 m for ADD versus 0.223 m for DeepMimic; DanceDB is 0.044/0.045 m and LaFAN1 is 0.028/0.029 m. On Run, ADD obtains 0.165 m versus DeepMimic's 0.013 m, and Sideflip/Roll exhibit local optima, showing that learned aggregation does not guarantee task-relevant trade-offs.

Training/deployment boundary: training requires reference motions, the physics simulator, ADD, critic, PPO/GAE, replay storage, and gradient regularization. In inference, only the current state, synchronized reference pose, frozen actor, and PD controller remain; ADD and tracking-differential computation are removed. All reported results are simulated, with no system identification, domain randomization, latency/noise model, or real-robot evidence.

Comparison boundary: ADD and DeepMimic are both frame-synchronous reference-conditioned trackers and mainly differ in reward scalarization. AMP instead discriminates expert and policy transition distributions without requiring alignment to a specified reference frame. Evaluating AMP with per-frame tracking errors inherently favors ADD/DeepMimic and cannot support a claim that ADD is a generally stronger adversarial imitation method.

zh.title: Learning Quadrupedal Locomotion over Challenging Terrain
zh.authors: Joonho Lee, Jemin Hwangbo, Lorenz Wellhausen, Vladlen Koltun, Marco Hutter
zh.institutions: Robotic Systems Lab, ETH Zurich; Robotics and Artificial Intelligence Lab, KAIST; Intelligent Systems Lab, Intel
